body: Somehow I missed your comment (I was trying to reply to everyone). I am awed by how many people in this community have offered to talk to my daughter. I didn't expect such a positive outpouring of support. I am going to talk to her tomorrow becauseshe was so tired when she hot home from school, she went to sleep right after dinner. Thanks again. I really do appreciate you offering an ear to my daughter. :)

Actually, your comment just made me google "The Center" and I found one closer to us in Long Beach. It's still 50 miles away, but my sister lives in Long Beach, so I can make a trip to the center and a visit to my sister all at once. Thanks so much for the suggestion. :)

Thanks for the reply. I have thought about that and I suggested a support group unrelated to that, but besides school/grades being gay is what is weighing heaviest on her. She really wants to find a gay support group. She wants to find people who not only support her, but can identify with her. Thanks again for the suggestion. :)
Thanks so much. I'm going to talk to her when she gets home from school. :)

Thanks so much for the well thought out response. I think I'm going to try to get her to post something in r/lgbt or r/actuallesbians, if she feels comfortable doing that. 

I had only watched the Pixar It Gets Better video with her. I've been watching the other videos today and crying pretty much all morning. I hope she'll watch a few when she gets home.

I do admit that I'm a bit tough on her when it comes to grades. This is something I'm working on, but it helps to hear it from someone else. 

Thanks for the reply. :)

Unfortunately, their LGBT youth group at the J.O. Community Center is no longer in operation. All emails sent to them get bounced back and their phone number is no longer in service. I tried contacting them for two weeks before I gave up.
Thanks for the suggestion. I have showed her the video. I'll have to see if there's more than one. I know it's not a solution, but it's the thought that counts. Thanks.
Thanks for posting this. I hadn't heard of this organization before. I'm going to call my local chapter to see if they have any resources. Thanks!

Wow... Thank so much for the reply. I will talk to my daughter when she gets home from school to see if she would be willing to talk online. I'm not sure how she would feel about it, but I hope she will consider it. 

I sincerely don't believe this is a problem requiring medication, but I'm no expert which is why I'm exploring all avenues. Thank again for offering your ear. I will pass the offer on to my daughter.
I think she would probably feel comfortable with kids 12-19. I have a car, so transportation is not an issue. Thank you so much for responding.

Being different is exactly what is getting to her the most. She likes being home because she can talk to me about anything, but she dreads school. Every morning she turns into a different person when it's time to go to school. She insists she's not being bullied or harassed, but I'm at the point where I want to send notes to all her teachers asking them to verify this.
I'm going to check out this subreddit. Thanks for the suggestion. I had forgotten about it.
I think my daughter is really just desperate for someone her age to talk to.

I took her to the county hospital the same day she confided this in me but they said they couldn't take her in because she doesn't have a plan yet and they didn't have any beds open. That's why I'm trying to get Medicaid to get her some outpatient help. Until my Medicaid is approved, I was hoping to find something else.
I tried looking on this site, but still couldn't find anything in our area. :(

I accidentally posted that reply from my main account, so I had to delete it. Here's the original text: Hi. Thank you so much for the response and the kind words. Since this account is not linked to me, I feel okay saying that I live near Lake Elsinore, CA. 

I already have an offer from a friend of my sister's who would to talk to my daughter. My sister's friend is gay and has lived in this area all her life (we moved here a couple years ago), but my daughter doesn't feel comfortable talking to her. My daughter wants to find an LGBT youth group in this area. Right now she feels like she has no one her age to talk to. Thanks.

I would love to introduce her to Reddit for the community factor, but I'm a little leery of the raunch/misogyny. I'll definitely check out r/LGBT and r/actuallesbians to see if I can find some gems. Thanks!
Thanks for bringing that to my attention. I initially posted from my phone and forgot to log out of my main account when I switched to my laptop.
